title: Derived direct image preserves direct sums
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Then the derived direct image $Rf_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image, def-pc-derived-category] commutes with all set-indexed direct sums.

proof.text: An isomorphism of sheaves on $Y$ can be checked on an affine open cover. Fix an affine $U\subseteq Y$, replace $Y$ by $U$ and $X$ by $f^{-1}U$, and choose a positive uniform bound $N$ from [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-uniform-truncation-bound]. For $T=\tau_{\leq -N-1}E$, the triangle $T\to E\to\tau_{\geq -N}E\to T[1]$ and the bound give $H^0(Rf_*T)=H^1(Rf_*T)=0$: indeed $T[-N-1]$ has no positive cohomology (as $H^m(T[-N-1])=H^{m-N-1}(T)$), so its direct image vanishes in degrees at least $N$, i.e. $H^j(Rf_*T)=H^{j+N+1}(Rf_*T[-N-1])=0$ for $j\geq-1$. Thus $H^0(Rf_*E)\cong H^0(Rf_*\tau_{\geq -N}E)$, naturally in $E$, for every member of the family and its direct sum. Truncation commutes with direct sums because cohomology sheaves do, so the same fixed $N$ reduces the degree-zero comparison to a family bounded below by $-N$.

source.place: Tag 08D5 proof, reduction to a quasi-compact target and truncation bound

proof.text: Apply the bounded-below truncation spectral sequence [thm-sp-truncation-e2] to the left exact functor $f_*$ and each $E_i$ and $E=\bigoplus_iE_i$: its natural $E_2$ page is $R^pf_*H^q(-)$ and its abutment is $H^{p+q}(Rf_*(-))$. On every affine $V\subseteq Y$, $f^{-1}V$ is a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme (quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of $f$ over the affine $V$); apply [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-cohomology-direct-sum] there to the quasi-coherent sheaves $H^q(E_i)|_{f^{-1}V}$. These compatible cohomology isomorphisms give an isomorphism of the associated presheaves on the affine basis; [lem-weil-pbc-higher-direct-image-presheaf] identifies their sheafifications with the higher direct images, and [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] identifies the direct sum sheaf with the sheafification of the sectionwise direct sums. Thus $\bigoplus_iR^pf_*H^q(E_i)\cong R^pf_*(\bigoplus_iH^q(E_i))$. Cohomology sheaves of complexes commute with direct sums, giving the comparison of the $E_2$ pages. In total degree zero, $q\geq-N$ and $p\geq0$, so only $0\leq p\leq N$ occurs. The natural finite filtrations and their associated graded isomorphisms from [thm-sp-truncation-e2] then show, by induction along the filtration, that $\bigoplus_iH^0(Rf_*E_i)\to H^0(Rf_*E)$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: The comparison map $\bigoplus_iRf_*E_i\to Rf_*(\bigoplus_iE_i)$ is an isomorphism on $H^0$ over every affine $U\subseteq Y$ by Steps 1 and 2, hence on $Y$. For each integer $k$, repeat those steps with the family $E_i[k]$; shifts commute with direct sums and $Rf_*$, so the original comparison is an isomorphism on $H^k$. A morphism of derived objects that is an isomorphism on every cohomology sheaf is an isomorphism. Both sides lie in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ by the definition of its direct sum and preservation of quasi-coherent cohomology under $Rf_*$ [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-preserves-qcoh].
